text:
dmitri: Quick idea 12 propose a policy-driven write-steering prototype using short-lived consent tokens + a soft-escrow handshake for PII tenants. Goal: deterministic active/active routing without full geo-locks.
kevin: sketch the handshake? how does this differ from our existing escrow ideas? :thinking:
maya: tl;dr: escrow here is minimal 12 a signed token asserting 'consent + region preference' from control plane. Dataplane uses it to accept writes locally or forward. no heavy state transfer.
nash: @dmitri question: what if tokens expire mid-swap? split-brain risk.
dmitri: plan: token carries expiry + "decay_ttl" metadata. proxies accept local writes if token present OR if last-seen token within decay window. after window, fall back to canonical consent lookup (slower) and possibly reroute.
kevin: availability vs correctness knob. decay window configurable per-tenant. some customers want strict residency (zero decay).
maya: add per-tenant policy: mode = {strict, preferred, permissive}. strict => no decay, forward to resident region only. preferred => short decay (30s). permissive => longer (5m).
nash: auditing concerns. legal will want traces for any cross-residency writes.
nash: emit an event 'write_routing_decision' with fields: tenant, request_id, origin_region, routed_region, reason=(token|decay|policy_fallback).
ops-bot: infra note 12 proxies must validate token signature locally (public key cache) and fallback to control-plane validation on miss. caching window required.
nash: crypto note 12 tokens should be ECDSA-signed and include tenant KMS key fingerprint to allow fast revocation.
kevin: perf Q: will this add latency on cold path? signature verify cheap but control-plane fallback heavy. need local cache hit >99.9%.
maya: pre-warm keys on tenant attach and push rotations. provide a verification helper for proxies.
dmitri: implementation sketch: 1) control plane issues consent token on tenant config changes. 2) client includes token in x-residency-consent header. 3) edge proxy validates; if valid and policy allows, serve locally. 4) if invalid/expired -> check cache -> if within decay_window allow with reason=decay. else call control-plane sync endpoint and emit audit event.
nash: edge case: shared models with different residency needs. model inference region must be checked; if mismatch deny.
kevin: add model-residency tag. tokens carry allowed_model_regions. otherwise deny.
maya: rollout: A) lab sim with synthetic PII tenants B) canary region permissive mode C) enable strict mode via admin gate.
dmitri: experiments: percent routed by decay vs token vs control-fallback; avg extra latency on fallback; audit event volume.
nash: failure if control-plane partitioned: proxies default conservative for strict tenants, permissive for dev/test. per-tenant default required.
kevin: also document operator runbook: revoke token fast, abort swap mid-flight, query audit traces.
maya: i'll draft an RFC summary + sequence diagrams tomorrow. tagging @ashley for legal review on audit semantics and retention. :+1:
nash: thanks. i'll spike next week to validate key cache hit assumptions unless objections.
ops-bot: reminder: create a feature-flag before canary.
nash: ack.
